name: Husqvarna Pickaroon
title: Husqvarna Pickaroon: Log Handling Hand Tool
meta: The Husqvarna pickaroon lets you hook, drag, flip and stack firewood rounds and small logs without bending over. How to use it, care tips and who it suits.
tagline: A one-hand pick for dragging, flipping and stacking rounds without bending down.
summary: The Husqvarna pickaroon is a short-handled pick that lets you grab, drag and toss firewood rounds and small logs without reaching down with your hands. It saves your back and fingers on any job where you are moving a lot of cut wood.
highlights: Sharp steel pick head bites into wood
Short handle for one-hand use
Saves bending and lifting on cleanup
Keeps hands away from splinters and pinch points
Useful for firewood, cordwood and brush cleanup
specs: Moving rounds, splits and small logs

body.h: What a pickaroon does on a tree job
p: After the saw work is done, someone has to move the wood. A pickaroon puts a hardened point on the end of a handle so you can stick a round, drag it to the pile and flip it into the truck or onto the stack without bending over for every piece. On a big cleanup that adds up to a lot less strain on your back.

It also keeps your hands out of the way. Rounds roll, splits have sharp edges and stacks shift. Hooking a piece from arm's length is safer than grabbing it, especially when you are loading a dump body or feeding a splitter all afternoon.

Swing the point into end grain or side grain with a short, controlled stroke, then pull. Work with the pile, not across your feet, and keep the point clear of your legs when you carry it. Do not use a pickaroon as a lever on big logs. That is a job for a peavey or cant hook.

Keep the point reasonably sharp with a file so it bites instead of glancing off, and check that the head is tight on the handle before each use. Check the listing for the current handle length and head design. For more tools for moving and stacking wood, see our log handling tools.

faq.q: Is a pickaroon the same as a hookaroon?
faq.a: The names are often used for the same thing: a pick on a handle for moving wood. Hookaroon usually means a longer handle, pickaroon a shorter one-hand tool.

faq.q: Can I roll big logs with a pickaroon?
faq.a: No. It is made for rounds, splits and small logs. Use a peavey or cant hook to roll and lever heavy logs.

name: LogRite Pickaroon
title: LogRite Pickaroon: Aluminum Handle Log Tool
meta: The LogRite pickaroon is a light hand tool for hooking, dragging and stacking firewood and small logs. See how crews use it and what to check before buying.
tagline: A light aluminum-handled pickaroon for crews that move wood every day.
summary: The LogRite pickaroon is a short pick on a lightweight aluminum handle, made for hooking, dragging and stacking rounds, splits and small logs. LogRite is known for its log handling tools, and this one is built for crews who move wood day after day.
highlights: Lightweight aluminum handle
Steel point for a solid bite in wood
One-hand tool for rounds and splits
Cuts down on bending and grabbing
Pairs well with a LogRite cant hook or peavey

body.h: Why crews like a LogRite pickaroon
p: A LogRite pickaroon is about not touching every piece of wood with your hands. Stick the point in a round, drag it to the pile, and toss it into the truck or onto the splitter table. On a cleanup with a few cords of wood on the ground, that saves your back and keeps your fingers away from sharp edges and rolling rounds.
The aluminum handle keeps it light enough to swing all day, and it will not rot or loosen the way a wood handle can after a season in the truck.

It is a good match for firewood processing, cleanup after a removal, and any job where the crew is loading rounds into a dump trailer by hand. One worker with a pickaroon can keep pace with a saw far longer than one bending for every piece.

Use short, controlled swings and pull toward the pile, not across your legs. A pickaroon is a hooking tool, not a pry bar. When a log is too big to drag, switch to a cant hook or peavey. Check the listing for current lengths, since a longer handle gives more reach and a shorter one is quicker in tight spots.
Touch up the point with a file when it starts glancing off, and check that the head is secure before each job. See the rest of our log handling tools for cant hooks, peaveys and log lifters.

faq.q: Why choose an aluminum handle?
faq.a: Aluminum is light and does not rot, crack or swell in the weather the way wood can, so the tool stays tight and easy to swing.

faq.q: Can I replace the point?
faq.a: Check the listing and LogRite's information for replacement parts for your model before you buy.

name: Rope-Tek HitchHiker 2
title: Rope-Tek HitchHiker 2: Mechanical Climbing Device
meta: The Rope-Tek HitchHiker 2 is a mechanical climbing device for arborists who want smooth slack tending and control. What it does, who it suits and safety notes.
tagline: A mechanical device from Rope-Tek for climbers who want easy slack tending and control.
summary: The Rope-Tek HitchHiker 2 is a mechanical climbing device for tree climbers who want smooth slack tending and fine control in the canopy. It is aimed at experienced climbers moving away from a plain friction hitch toward a more mechanical setup.
highlights: Mechanical device for arborist climbing systems
Smooth slack tending as you advance
Fine control when working and descending
Second generation of the HitchHiker design
Check the listing for rope compatibility and setup

p: Climbers search for the HitchHiker 2 when they want something between a friction hitch and a fully mechanical device: the familiar feel of a hitch-based system with less fiddling, better slack tending and consistent behavior from one climb to the next. It sits in the same part of the gear shop as the Petzl Zigzag and similar devices.

Exact configuration, rope diameter range and the systems it is approved for come from Rope-Tek, so read the instructions and the listing before you build your system around it. Compare it with other devices for MRS to see what suits the way you climb.

Mechanical devices change how a climbing system feels compared with a friction hitch. Expect a learning period: how the device grabs, how it releases, and how much input it needs to descend smoothly will all feel different at first. Give yourself time on the ground and at low height to learn its habits before working with a saw.

Any device in your life-support system has to be used exactly as the manufacturer describes, with compatible rope and connectors, and in line with ANSI Z133 and your employer's procedures. Learn it low and slow, close to the ground, with a trained climber who knows the device before you take it aloft.
Inspect it before every climb for wear, cracks, bent parts and smooth movement, and keep it clean of sap and grit. Retire it if it has taken a big load or shows damage.

faq.q: Is the HitchHiker 2 for MRS or SRS?
faq.a: Check Rope-Tek's instructions for the systems and configurations it is approved for. Do not use it in any setup the instructions do not cover.

faq.q: What rope does it need?
faq.a: Use only rope diameters and types the manufacturer lists as compatible. Rope that is too thin, thick or stiff changes how any device grips.

name: Petzl ZIGZAG PLUS Mechanical Prusik
title: Petzl ZIGZAG PLUS Mechanical Prusik for Arborists
meta: The Petzl ZIGZAG PLUS is a mechanical prusik for tree climbers, built on the Zigzag with added friction control. How it compares, who it suits and care tips.
tagline: Petzl's mechanical prusik with extra friction control for tree climbers.
summary: The Petzl ZIGZAG PLUS is a mechanical prusik for arborists that builds on the original Zigzag with an added friction element, so it can be set up for a wider range of climbing systems. Climbers choose it for the smooth, precise descent control the Zigzag is known for.
highlights: Mechanical prusik built on the Zigzag design
Added friction element for more control
Smooth, precise descent with the handle
Integrated pulley to tend slack
No hitch cord to tie or replace

body.h: How the ZIGZAG PLUS differs from the Zigzag
p: The standard Zigzag is a chain of links that replaces a friction hitch on a doubled rope. The ZIGZAG PLUS keeps that mechanism and adds an extra friction element, which gives more control and lets Petzl approve it for more ways of climbing. If you climb on more than one system, that flexibility is the main reason to pay the extra.

On the tree it behaves like a Zigzag: you advance it with the pulley, rest on it, and release with the handle for a controlled descent. Read Petzl's instructions for the exact configurations and rope types approved. See other devices for MRS to compare.

Rope choice matters with any mechanical prusik. Use only ropes within Petzl's listed range, and expect the feel to change with rope diameter, cover and wear. Practice close to the ground with a trained climber before you take it aloft, and follow ANSI Z133 and your company's procedures.

Inspect it before every climb: check the links and pulley for wear and grooving, make sure everything moves freely, and clean out sap and grit. Retire it if parts are worn past Petzl's limits or it has been shock loaded.

Keep a record of when you put it into service and how much use it gets, and replace worn parts or the whole device as Petzl's instructions describe. A mechanical prusik is precise but only as good as its condition.

faq.q: Should I buy the Zigzag or the ZIGZAG PLUS?
faq.a: If you only climb on a doubled rope, the standard Zigzag may be all you need. The PLUS adds friction control and wider approved use, so it suits climbers who switch systems.

faq.q: Do I still need a hitch cord?
faq.a: No. The links replace the friction hitch. You still need compatible rope, connectors and a properly set up system.

name: Boom Lift Shock-Absorbing Lanyard
title: Boom Lift Lanyard: Shock-Absorbing Fall Arrest
meta: A boom lift lanyard connects your harness to the platform anchor and absorbs energy in a fall. Choosing the right length, fit and standards for aerial lifts.
tagline: A shock-absorbing lanyard for connecting to the anchor in a boom lift or bucket.
summary: A boom lift lanyard connects your full body harness to the anchor point in an aerial lift platform, and its shock absorber reduces the force on your body if you are thrown or fall from the basket. It is required personal protective equipment on most boom lift and bucket truck work.
highlights: Shock-absorbing pack reduces fall forces
Connects harness to the platform anchor
Snap hooks for harness and anchor
For boom lifts and bucket trucks
Check listing for length and ratings

body.h: Why you tie in at the platform
p: On a boom lift or bucket truck, a bump, a pothole or a sudden boom movement can catapult you out of the basket. A lanyard attached to the manufacturer's anchor point keeps you with the platform, and the shock absorber limits the force on your body if it catches you.
Shorter lanyards keep you from going over the rail at all, which is better than arresting a fall. Pick the shortest length that lets you work, and never tie off to the boom, a tree or a nearby pole.

On a bucket truck, the same applies: anchor to the point the manufacturer provides inside the bucket or on the boom tip, as the lift manual describes. Keep the lanyard routed so it cannot snag controls or get caught by the boom as it moves.

Use a lanyard that meets the standards your employer and the lift manufacturer require, and connect it to a full body harness at the back D-ring unless instructions say otherwise. Check the listing for length, connector type and ratings before buying, and confirm clearance requirements for your lift.

Inspect webbing, stitching, the shock pack and snap hooks before each use. Retire any lanyard that has arrested a fall or shows damage. Follow ANSI Z133, OSHA and your training. See more fall arrest for aerial lifts.

faq.q: Can I use my climbing lanyard in a bucket?
faq.a: No. Aerial lift fall protection uses a full body harness and a lanyard rated for that use, attached to the lift's designated anchor.

faq.q: How long should a boom lift lanyard be?
faq.a: As short as practical. A shorter lanyard limits how far you can move toward the rail. Check the lift manual for anchor and clearance guidance.

name: ArborMats Ground Protection Mat
title: ArborMats Ground Protection Mat for Tree Crews
meta: ArborMats ground protection mats give trucks, lifts and stump grinders a temporary road over lawns and soft ground. How tree crews use them and what to check.
tagline: Ground mats that keep trucks and machines from rutting lawns on tree jobs.
summary: ArborMats are ground protection mats that tree crews lay down as a temporary road for trucks, lifts, loaders and stump grinders. They spread the load so you can cross lawns and soft ground without leaving ruts for the customer to look at.
highlights: Temporary roadway over turf and soft ground
Spreads load from trucks and equipment
Traction surface for tires and tracks
Reusable from job to job
Check listing for size and load rating

body.h: Why mats pay off on residential work
p: Getting a lift or a loaded chip truck into a back yard is often what makes a removal profitable. Leaving deep ruts in the lawn is what loses the next job. ArborMats spread the weight of tires and tracks over a larger area so soft ground holds up, and the crew leaves a yard that needs a rake, not a regrade.
Mats also protect pavers, irrigation heads and septic areas, and give the crew a cleaner, less slippery surface to work on in the wet.

Mats also make a difference on commercial and municipal jobs, where a crew might be crossing sports fields, cemeteries or landscaped medians. A clean exit keeps property managers happy and avoids repair bills that eat into the job's margin.

Plan the route before the equipment arrives, lay mats ahead of the machine and overlap or connect them so edges do not lift. Check the listing for size, weight and load rating, and make sure the rating suits your heaviest machine.

Lift mats with enough people or with equipment, and keep your feet clear when setting them down. Hose them off before loading so you do not track mud to the next site. Compare other ground protection mats.
Stack and strap them securely on the trailer.

faq.q: Will ArborMats hold a bucket truck?
faq.a: Check the load rating on the listing against your truck's weight and how it will be set up, including outrigger pads.

faq.q: Can I put outriggers on a mat?
faq.a: Use outrigger pads made for that purpose and follow the lift manufacturer's setup instructions.

name: Husqvarna Chainsaw Hat
title: Husqvarna Chainsaw Hat: Saw Logo Cap
meta: A Husqvarna chainsaw hat for saw users and tree crews, for wear at the shop, the truck or around town. Fit, style and why it is not a substitute for a helmet.
tagline: A Husqvarna saw cap for the shop, the truck and days off.
summary: The Husqvarna chainsaw hat is a branded cap for anyone who runs Husqvarna saws, from tree crews to firewood cutters. It is made for everyday wear at the shop, on the drive and around town.
highlights: Husqvarna chainsaw branding
Everyday cap for saw users
Adjustable fit (check listing)
Good gift for a saw fan
Off-job wear, not head protection

p: Plenty of tree workers run orange saws and are happy to say so. The Husqvarna chainsaw hat is a simple way to do that. Wear it in the shop while you sharpen chains, on the drive between jobs or on the weekend.
Check the listing for the current design, colors and closure, since Husqvarna updates its apparel line regularly. See more hats and caps from saw and arborist brands.
Husqvarna has been making chainsaws for decades and its saws are a fixture on tree crews and in firewood yards. A logo cap is a simple way to show which saws you trust on the job.

A cap is not head protection. When you run a chainsaw, climb or work under a tree, wear a helmet that meets the required standard, with eye and hearing protection. Keep the cap for the truck and the shop.
Cool, dry cotton or a mesh-back cap is comfortable in summer. In cold weather, a helmet liner under your helmet is the better choice on the job.

On the job, a cap can work under a hood or in the truck on a cold morning. Wash it as the label says to keep its shape, and keep a spare in the truck so you are not stuck with a sweaty one at the end of a long day.

faq.q: Is the hat adjustable?
faq.a: Most styles have an adjustable back. Check the listing for the closure on the current version.

faq.q: Can I wear it under my helmet?
faq.a: A brimmed cap will interfere with helmet fit. Use a thin helmet liner instead.

name: Rock Exotica Hat
title: Rock Exotica Hat: Logo Cap for Climbers
meta: The Rock Exotica hat is a cap for climbers and riggers who know the brand's pulleys and hardware. For the shop, the truck and days off, not for climbing in.
tagline: A Rock Exotica logo cap for rope and hardware nerds.
summary: The Rock Exotica hat is a logo cap for climbers, riggers and rope access workers who know the brand's pulleys, swivels and connectors. It is an everyday cap for the shop, the truck and days off.
highlights: Rock Exotica branding
Everyday cap for climbers and riggers
Check listing for style and fit
Good gift for a gear fan
Off-job wear, not head protection

body.h: For people who know the hardware
p: Rock Exotica makes hardware that shows up on a lot of arborist saddles and rigging setups, from pulleys to swivels and connectors. The Rock Exotica hat is for climbers who like the brand and want to wear it off the rope.
Check the listing for the current style, colors and closure. See more hats and caps for the crew.

It also suits rope access techs, rescue teams and anyone who spends time around rope systems. A cap is an easy gift for a climber who already has every pulley and swivel they want, and a way to spot gear people at a climbing event.

A cap is comfortable in the shop, at a climbing competition or on the drive home, but it is not head protection. In the tree or under it, wear a helmet that meets the required standard, with eye and hearing protection as needed.
In cold weather, a thin helmet liner keeps your head warm under a climbing helmet without upsetting the fit.
Wash it per the label to keep its shape, and keep it in the truck for the end of the day when the helmet comes off. A cap with a brim also helps keep sun off your face on the drive and at lunch.

faq.q: Is it adjustable?
faq.a: Check the listing for the closure and sizing on the current version.

faq.q: Can I wear it under a helmet?
faq.a: A brimmed cap interferes with helmet fit. Use a helmet liner instead.

name: Husqvarna X-COM R Headset
title: Husqvarna X-COM R Headset: Hearing and Crew Comms
meta: The Husqvarna X-COM R headset combines hearing protection with crew communication so climbers and ground crew can talk over the saw. Features, fit and care.
tagline: Hearing protection with crew radio built in, so the climber and ground can talk.
summary: The Husqvarna X-COM R headset is hearing protection with built-in crew communication, part of the Husqvarna X-COM line. It lets a climber and ground crew talk in a normal voice over a running saw or chipper instead of shouting and waving.
highlights: Hearing protection with integrated crew comms
Talk between climber and ground over the saw
Phone connection (check listing)
Rechargeable battery
Check listing for helmet or headband mount

body.h: Why crew comms change the job
p: Most rigging problems start with a missed call. The climber says hold, the groundie hears let it run. With an X-COM headset, both can talk in a normal voice over a saw, a chipper or traffic, so lowering, felling and drop zone calls are clear the first time.

The X-COM R adds a built-in radio to Husqvarna's communication hearing protection. Check the listing for radio type, range, phone pairing and whether it mounts to a helmet or a headband, and make sure the whole crew is on compatible units. See more communication gear.

Hearing protection only works if it seals. Fit the cups over your ears with no hair, glasses arms or hood in the way, and check the noise rating against your saws and chipper. Charge it each night so it does not die halfway through a removal.

Comms do not replace a clear plan. Agree on commands before the job starts, use a backup signal if a unit drops out, and follow ANSI Z133 communication requirements. Inspect cushions and replace them when they crack or stiffen.

Keep units clean and dry, store them out of direct sun, and keep the firmware current if the listing or Husqvarna's instructions call for it. Label each headset so crew members keep their own cushions and fit.

faq.q: What is the difference between X-COM R and X-COM Active?
faq.a: The R adds a built-in radio. Check the listings for current features of each before choosing.

faq.q: Does it work with other brands of headset?
faq.a: Compatibility depends on the radio system. Check the listing, and test the full crew setup before relying on it on a job.

name: Throwball Kit
title: Throwball Kit: Throw Weight and Line for Arborists
meta: A throwball kit gives you throw weights, throw line and storage in one bag for setting climbing lines and rigging points. What to look for and how to use one.
tagline: Throw weights, line and storage in one kit for setting lines in the canopy.
summary: A throwball kit bundles throw weights, throw line and storage so you can set climbing and rigging lines high in the canopy without hunting for parts. It is the quickest way to get a complete, matched setup for line setting.
highlights: Throw weights and throw line in one package
Storage keeps the line tangle-free
For setting climbing lines and rigging points
Good starter set for new climbers
Check listing for weights, line length and bag
specs: Throw weights, throw line and storage (check listing)

p: Setting a good tie-in point starts with a clean throw. A kit gives you weights and line that work together, plus a bag or cube that lets the line pay out without knots. For a new climber, or a crew replacing a tangled mess, it is the simplest way to get set up.

Check the listing for what comes in this kit: the weight of the throw bags or balls, the line length and diameter, and the storage. Lighter weights suit small branches and thin forks; heavier ones carry line higher and through dense canopy. See more throw line kits.

A kit also makes it easy to set up a second throw line for the crew truck, or to have a backup on hand when a line gets stuck in the canopy. Many climbers keep one kit with a lighter weight for small branches and a heavier one for tall trees.
Clear the drop zone before every throw. A throw weight coming back down can injure someone, and line can catch on deadwood or near power lines. Never throw near energized conductors.

Flake the line into its bag after each use, inspect it for cuts and glazing, and replace weights with torn covers or loose rings. Once the line is set, pull your climbing rope through and test the tie-in point before you load it.
Practice your throws on the ground to build accuracy.

faq.q: What weight throw bag should I use?
faq.a: Many climbers carry two: a lighter one for small crotches and a heavier one for height. Check the listing for weights included.

faq.q: Can I use throw line for rigging?
faq.a: No. Throw line is only for pulling a rope into place. Never climb or lower loads on it.

name: WD-40 Specialist Dry Graphite Lube
title: WD-40 Graphite Dry Lube for Locks and Hardware
meta: WD-40 graphite dry lube leaves a dry film that keeps locks, hinges and hardware moving without attracting sawdust and grit. Uses, cautions and what to avoid.
tagline: A dry graphite lube for locks, hinges and hardware that should not get gummy.
summary: WD-40 graphite dry lube from the Specialist line sprays on wet and dries to a graphite film, keeping locks, hinges and small mechanisms moving without the sticky residue that attracts sawdust and grit. It suits the truck, trailer and shop where wet oil just collects dirt.
highlights: Dries to a graphite film
Less sticky residue to collect dust and chips
Good for locks, latches and hinges
Handy in dusty, sawdust-heavy settings
Read the label for compatible materials

body.h: Why a dry lube on a tree crew
p: Saw work fills everything with dust and chips. Oil on a padlock, a tool box latch or a trailer hinge turns that dust into paste. A dry graphite lube goes on as a spray, the carrier evaporates, and a dry film is left behind that keeps parts moving without collecting gunk.
Use it on padlocks, truck box and trailer locks, hinges and other metal mechanisms in the shop and on the trucks. See more chainsaw and shop fluids.

Graphite lubes are an old shop standard for locks because graphite stays slick without being sticky. Shake the can well, spray a small amount into the lock or joint, work the mechanism a few times and let it dry before use. A little goes a long way.

Keep lubricants off ropes, slings, saddles and other textiles, and off friction surfaces that need grip. For life-support hardware such as carabiners and pulleys, follow the manufacturer's care instructions: many recommend cleaning in water and using only a lubricant they approve, applied sparingly and wiped clean.
It is not a bar and chain oil or a replacement for engine lubricants. Use the spray in a ventilated area, keep it away from heat and flame, and read the label before use.
Graphite can mark fabric and paint, so mask off or wipe away overspray. Store the can upright, out of the sun and away from the cab heater.

faq.q: Can I use graphite lube on carabiner gates?
faq.a: Check the carabiner maker's instructions first. Some approve light lubrication of the gate hinge; keep any lube away from rope contact areas and wipe off the excess.

faq.q: Is it the same as regular WD-40?
faq.a: No. Regular WD-40 is a wet multi-use product. The dry graphite lube is made to leave a dry film.

name: Husqvarna 372XP Felling Dogs
title: Husqvarna 372XP Felling Dogs: Replacement Spikes
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 372XP felling dogs give the saw a solid pivot against the log for bucking and felling. Fitment, install tips and when to replace them.
tagline: Replacement bumper spikes that give the 372XP a solid pivot in big wood.
summary: Husqvarna 372XP felling dogs replace worn, bent or missing bumper spikes on the 372XP. Sharp felling dogs give the saw a pivot point against the log, so you can lever through big cuts with less effort and more control.
highlights: Replacement felling dogs for the 372XP
Pivot point for bucking and felling
Replace bent or dull spikes
Bolt-on installation
Check listing for inner or outer dog

p: Felling dogs are the toothed spikes beside the bar. Set them into the wood and the saw pivots on them, so the bar walks through the cut with less push from you. On a 372XP bucking big rounds or cutting a felling notch, a solid set of dogs makes the saw feel stronger and steadier.
Dogs bend when the saw is dropped or pinched, and the points wear round after hard use. When they slip instead of biting, it is time to replace them.

The 372XP is a long-running pro saw, and many crews keep older units in service with good parts. Felling dogs are among the cheapest parts to replace and among the most noticeable when they are worn. If you also have bent bar studs or a cracked clutch cover from the same drop, fix those at the same time.

Check the listing for whether this is an inner or outer dog, or a set, and match it to your saw and any fitted options. Remove the bar and chain, take off the old dog, and fit the new one with the correct screws, tightened firmly. Make sure nothing rubs the chain.
Use genuine or listed compatible parts. See more power equipment parts for your saws.
Check that the dogs sit flat against the saw body and that the screws are secure after the first tank of fuel, since new parts can settle in.

faq.q: Will 372XP felling dogs fit other models?
faq.a: Some Husqvarna saws share parts, but check the part number on the listing against your saw before ordering.

faq.q: Do I need special tools?
faq.a: Usually just the screwdriver or Torx bit for the dog screws, plus your scrench for the bar nuts.

name: Husqvarna 562XP Felling Dogs
title: Husqvarna 562XP Felling Dogs: Replacement Spikes
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 562XP felling dogs restore a firm pivot point for bucking and felling with your 562XP. Fitment notes, install steps and when to replace.
tagline: Replacement bumper spikes for the 562XP so the saw bites and pivots cleanly.
summary: Husqvarna 562XP felling dogs replace the worn or bent bumper spikes on a 562XP. A sharp set gives the saw a firm pivot against the wood, which makes bucking and felling cuts smoother and less tiring.
highlights: Replacement felling dogs for the 562XP
Firm pivot for bucking and felling
Replace bent or rounded spikes
Bolt-on installation
Check listing for inner or outer dog

p: The 562XP is a workhorse for felling and bucking on tree crews. When its felling dogs are bent or worn smooth, the saw slips instead of pivoting, and you end up pushing the bar through the cut. That wastes time, wears you out and makes it harder to keep a straight cut.
Replacing the dogs is a quick, cheap fix that brings back the bite and the leverage.

Bent dogs often come from the saw being dropped, getting caught in a pinch or bouncing off a log. Look them over whenever you clean the saw. A loose dog can also rattle, wear the mounting holes and eventually let the screws back out, so tighten them as part of routine maintenance.

Check the listing for whether this is an inner dog, an outer dog or a set, and confirm the part number for your saw. Remove the bar and chain, take off the old dog, fit the new one with the right screws and tighten them well. Make sure the chain runs clear.
While you are there, check the chain catcher and clutch cover. See more power equipment parts for the 562XP and other saws.
Keep a spare set in the parts box so a bent dog does not take a good saw out of service on a busy day.

faq.q: Can I fit bigger felling dogs on a 562XP?
faq.a: Aftermarket dogs exist for many saws. Check that any part is made for your model and does not interfere with the chain or cover.

faq.q: How often should I replace them?
faq.a: When they are bent, loose or worn so they no longer bite. Check them whenever you clean the saw.
